elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "any other materials, work product or deliverables prepared by TrueLink for Client under this Agreement shall be the exclusive property of Client"

elements.element: Vendor assigns those rights to Customer
elements.evidence: "TrueLink hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest therein"
"TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface" (untouched 2(d))

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "to the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded in such results, TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, the Credit Data and all other data submitted by or on behalf of Client"
"no item is jointly owned by the parties"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: Insertion addresses only the Interface retention in 2(d); no generic tools or know-how carve-out appears.

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables
elements.evidence: Licence is limited to embedded TrueLink IP "as part of such results", not a licence to deliverables as such (Customer instead owns them).

offending_extra_words: in the ordinary course of Client's business
reasons: All preferred atomic elements are satisfied: Vendor assignment of deliverables/work product, Vendor's retained ownership of the Interface left intact, a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor IP, Customer retention of Customer Data and IP, and an express no-joint-ownership statement.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no generic tools/know-how ownership term and no licence to deliverables), but that is immaterial because the locked target is preferred and preferred is met.

Minimality fails: the embedded-IP licence imports fallback-only scope words "worldwide" and "modify and sublicense", plus the extra qualifier "in the ordinary course of Client's business", which are not needed to complete the preferred position (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free).

Intent is preserved: the Vendor's Interface ownership, confidentiality provisions and the term/renewal mechanics are untouched, and the cross-reference to the Section 8(d) licence avoids contradiction with the existing data licence.
